observations.explanation: The paper evaluates HotpotQA, Fever, ALFWorld, and WebShop (PDF pp. 3, 7–8). On both knowledge tasks, the combined methods beat standalone CoT-SC and ReAct in the reported results (p. 6).

For ALFWorld, the paper says Act prompts use the same annotated trajectories without thoughts and that six prompt permutations provide a controlled comparison (p. 7). The best ReAct trial scores 71% versus 45% for the best Act trial (pp. 7–8).
The paper reports reasoning errors for ReAct and says non-informative search results account for 23% of error cases and can derail its trajectory (PDF p. 6).

The conclusion notes that complex tasks with large action spaces need more demonstrations, which can exceed in-context input limits, and describes fine-tuning as having initial promising results (PDF p. 10).
